When the number of in-use connections reaches maxPoolSize, the next request waits, so raising it supports more concurrent requests (and the tuning guide advises raising it when database load is low and few connections are active). If database CPU is higher than expected and logs show more connection attempts than expected, decrease maxPoolSize or reduce application threads. edits.old: maxConnecting is separate from maxPoolSize: it limits how many connections one pool may establish concurrently, while maxPoolSize limits the pool's total application connections. Raising maxConnecting allows a pool to replenish sockets faster; use it when measured connection setup time is the bottleneck. (high confidence)
edits.new: maxConnecting is separate from maxPoolSize: it is the maximum number of connections a pool may be establishing concurrently (default 2), while maxPoolSize is the maximum number of connections opened in the pool. Raising maxConnecting lets the client establish connections to the server faster but increases the chance of connection storms; too low a value can cause heavy throttling and increased tail latency for clients checking out connections. maxConnecting is supported by all drivers except the Rust driver per the manual overview, although the Rust driver guide lists max_connecting. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/connection-pool-overview.md
